subject: Dedicated capacity — autoscaling, integration & next steps
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up from today's demo — dedicated capacity questions

Thanks for the demo this morning — nice product and clear performance numbers. A few follow-ups from our side as we evaluate Dedicated capacity: autoscaling behavior, throughput sizing, and integration details. High-level asks: 

- Can you share a recommended autoscaling policy and queue sizing guidance for predictable peak traffic?
- SDK/Auth: what's the best practice for server-to-server auth (service accounts vs API keys) and any VPC/private deployment constraints?
- Routing/structured output: we use tool-calling and structured JSON outputs — how does Redwood guarantee stability when routing between model variants / fallbacks?
- Embeddings + reranker: we'll batch embeddings and run a lightweight reranker — what are expected throughput/cost tradeoffs?

We ran some quick numbers internally (very preliminary): peak steady qps ~200, peak concurrent requests ~50, average input+output ~300 tokens, embeddings calls ~20k/day but with spikes. Latency target is p95 <= 500ms for single-turn generation. 

Can we get a post-call recap + next steps (mutual action plan) and any sizing template you typically use?

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Head of ML, Acme AI

Emily — thanks for the quick follow. Really appreciate the numbers, that helps a lot. I ran this past our Solutions team and put together a short mutual action plan + a sizing template (attached) to capture the workload details we need to recommend autoscaling and pool sizing. Action items below: 

- Acme (you): fill the attached sizing template with typical request distribution (RPS by time window), token sizes (prompt/response), model versions you plan to use, and embedding QPS by burst window.
- Redwood (we): draft recommended Dedicated pool size + autoscaling policy, queue sizing, and a brief architecture diagram showing routing/fallbacks and VPC options (we'll attach a diagram for your infra team).
- Schedule: propose 60-min architecture workshop next week (we'll bring Solutions + Infra). Please suggest 2x time slots.

Quick notes on the items you listed:
- Auth: service accounts (short-lived tokens) + mTLS into VPC is preferred for Private deployments; for Hosted/Dedicated we support customer-managed API keys + optional KMS integration. We'll include code snippets in the sizing template.
- Routing/structured output: we surface model variants as routable endpoints and provide automatic fallback policies (e.g., model X -> model Y) — structured output and tool-calling are preserved at the API layer; we'll summarize compatibility notes in the doc.
- Embeddings/reranker: common pattern is to batch embeddings async and run a small CPU-based reranker; we'll call out recommended batch sizes and a cost estimate column in the template.

Attached: acme-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (fill and return). I'll loop Aditya to provide technical guidance on queue sizing and throughput.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — attached is a first pass against the template (see summary below). Will bring our infra lead to the workshop if helpful.

Summary (prelim):
- Peak steady qps: 200 (90% of peak), peak bursts up to 350 qps for short windows (~2-3 minutes)
- Peak concurrent requests: 50 sustained, spikes up to 120 during batch ingestion windows
- Avg tokens (prompt + response): 300 (response typically ~180 tokens)
- Primary model: open-llama-70b (quantized), fallback to 13b in case of capacity constraints
- Embeddings: ~20k/day, but batch spikes up to 10k embeddings in a 5-minute window during nightly indexing
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 500ms for single-turn; background jobs can be relaxed

We also have procurement questions: what's the typical committed capacity granularity (per-GPU pools vs vCPU-equivalent blocks)? Will need to involve procurement after workshop.

Let us know available workshop times next Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Emily

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Feb 2027 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — dedicated capacity questions

Emily — thanks for the numbers, this is helpful. A few technical recommendations up-front (high-level; we can validate with workshop and exact token histograms):

1) Autoscaling & pool sizing
- For a steady 200 qps with spikes to 350 and concurrency up to 120, we recommend a Dedicated GPU pool sized to support the 200 qps baseline with autoscaling headroom to 1.8-2x baseline for burst capacity. Practically that looks like provisioning N GPUs where N = ceil(baseline_tokens_per_sec / per-GPU_throughput) — we'll compute once we have token distributions.
- Autoscaling policy: scale on queue length + token-throughput (not just request count). Use a two-tier policy: rapid scale for short bursts (min step + cooldown) and slower scale for sustained increases.

2) Concurrency & queue sizing
- Concurrency per GPU: depends on model and quantization. Example: quantized 70B on A100 may support 6-8 concurrent streams at p95 400-600ms; smaller models allow higher concurrency.
- Queue sizing: keep an incoming request queue that can buffer at least 2x peak burst for very short spikes (e.g., 700 QPS-buffer equivalent) and apply early rejection for requests that exceed latency SLO.

3) Routing & fallback
- Route by policy: latency-first requests go to pinned low-latency variants; best-effort route to cost-optimized variants. Automatic fallback preserves structured-tool calling semantics; payloads are validated at the API layer before routing.

4) Auth & network
- For Dedicated (customer-managed network): we support service accounts + mutual TLS; for Hosted Dedicated we can provision customer-scoped API keys with KMS-wrapped secrets. VPC peering + Private Link options available.

I'll attach a short architecture diagram and a rough sizing worksheet (pdf) that shows example per-GPU throughput assumptions and how we translate your numbers into pool size. We'll refine in the workshop.

Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — SDK snippets & quickstart

Emily — quick SDK notes and snippet to help your infra team prototype authentication and a simple routing call. Also pointing to our SDK quickstart in case you want to test locally before the workshop.

Auth (recommended): create a service account in your tenant and issue short-lived tokens via our token exchange endpoint. For Dedicated private deployments you can use mTLS client certs in front of the ingress.

Example (pseudo-code):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token-exchange \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service_account_id":"svc-acme-01","signed_jwt":"<signed-jwt>"}'
  # returns short-lived access_token (30m)

# call generation endpoint with model routing header
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Model: open-llama-70b-pinned" \
  -d '{"input":"...","tool_calls": [{"name":"qa_retriever","args":{}}]}' \
  https://dedicated-us.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Embeddings batching: use our async embeddings endpoint and batch up to 512 vectors per request for cost-efficiency. For reranking, we recommend running the initial recall on CPU (FAISS) and then a small transformer-based reranker on the Dedicated pool for top-K re-ranks.

SDK quickstart: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/architecture-acme (I've added a short HOWTO).

Dev Patel
Developer Advocate, Redwood Inference

Emily — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the filled template, team notes below and proposed next steps.

What we agreed (summary):
- Redwood to propose Dedicated pool sizing and autoscaling policy based on your token histogram; preliminary recommend: baseline pool sized for 200 qps with autoscale capacity to cover 350 qps bursts (we'll return numbers after we run the worksheet).
- Queue & concurrency: we'll use queue-length and token-throughput based scaling; recommend buffer for 2x burst and early reject to preserve your p95 SLO.
- Auth/network: service account + short-lived tokens for Hosted/Dedicated; mTLS + VPC peering option for Private deployment.
- Structured output/tool-calling: preserved through routing; we'll document any model-compat limitations and include test vectors.
- Embeddings/reranker: suggested flow — batch embeddings (async) -> FAISS recall -> Dedicated rerank for top-K. We'll include cost/throughput tradeoffs in the worksheet.

Next steps:
1) Redwood: finalize sizing calc and send updated worksheet + architecture PDF (attached) by EOD Fri 2/12.
2) Acme: confirm 2x workshop slots Tue 2/16 1:00-2:00pm PST or Wed 2/17 3:00-4:00pm PST and share any additional token histograms you want us to consider.
3) Procurement: we'll include committed capacity options in the follow-up SOW (DocuSign link included in related links).

Please reply with the preferred workshop slot and we'll lock in the invites. Looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
